media.title: Conserver et Gérer les Récoltes : Méthodes et Bonnes Pratiques
Discussion autour de la gestion et de la conservation des récoltes
Harvest Preservation and Management Methods and Best Practices

pages.title: Module objective
pages.text:
This module aims to provide guidance on the best techniques to adopt for the **harvesting**, **storage** and **packing** of produce.

These techniques allow produce to retain all its quality.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Objectif du module

pages.title: Harvesting, storing, packing
pages.text: Discover the essential practices, from the field to storage and transport, to preserve the freshness and value of your harvests.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Récolter, conserver, conditionner

pages.title: The three key words of the module
pages.text:
Before starting, it is important to clearly understand the three key words of this module:

- **Harvesting**: picking fruits or vegetables at the right time, without damaging them.
- **Storing**: keeping produce in good conditions so that it stays fresh longer.
- **Packing**: washing, sorting and packaging produce so that it can be easily sold, transported or stored.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les trois mots clés du module

pages.title: Required equipment
pages.text:
You will need the following equipment:

- Pruning shears or scissors, depending on the crop.
- Buckets, crates or plastic baskets.
- Shelves for storage.
- Washing basins.
- Cloths.
- Labels.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Matériel nécessaire

pages.title: Step 1: Harvest at the right time and with the right handling
pages.text: First step: learn to recognize optimal maturity, to choose the cool hours of the day and to handle your vegetables without damaging them.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Étape 1 : Récolter au bon moment et avec les bons gestes

pages.title: Recognizing the maturity of produce
pages.text:
You must harvest when the fruit or vegetable is ripe. To do this, you need to observe several criteria:

- **Color**: it changes as the produce ripens.
- **Firmness**: by touching, you can feel whether the fruit is still hard or is beginning to soften.
- **Smell and sometimes taste**: a ripe fruit often has a pleasant smell, and a good taste if you can try it.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Reconnaître la maturité des produits

pages.title: Avoid harvesting too early or too late
pages.text:
- If you harvest **too early**, the produce is still hard and has no flavor.
- If you harvest **too late**, it risks being damaged and difficult to sell.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Éviter de récolter trop tôt ou trop tard

pages.title: Choosing the right time of day
pages.text:
Always harvest **early in the morning** or **at the end of the day**, when it is cooler.

Coolness helps your harvests keep better.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Choisir le bon moment de la journée

pages.title: Adopting good harvesting practices
pages.text:
- Use your hands or clean, well-sharpened tools: pruning shears, scissors, etc.
- Cut or detach the vegetables with care.
- Place them gently in baskets or buckets, without throwing them.
- Avoid impacts and crushing.

The more carefully you harvest, the longer your produce will keep.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Adopter les bons gestes de récolte

pages.title: Sorting immediately after harvest
pages.text:
Once the harvest is finished, sort your produce right away: a rotten fruit can pass its mold on to the others.

Set aside damaged, spotted or overripe fruits or vegetables so that they do not spoil the rest of the harvest.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Trier immédiatement après la récolte

pages.title: Step 2: Wash and disinfect if needed
pages.text: Second step: clean your harvests under good hygienic conditions to ensure healthy, clean produce.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Étape 2 : Laver et désinfecter si besoin

pages.title: Washing with clean, potable water
pages.text:
Wash your vegetables with **clean, potable water**. Rub them gently to clean them thoroughly without damaging them.

⚠️ **Warning**: do not use water from canals or ponds, as it may be dirty and transmit diseases.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Laver à l’eau propre et potable

pages.title: Disinfecting when necessary
pages.text:
If you sell or store the produce, remember to disinfect it:

1. Add a few drops of **food-grade bleach** to a bucket of clean water.
2. Then rinse thoroughly with **clean, potable water**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Désinfecter si nécessaire

pages.title: Setting up a cleaning station
pages.text:
To prevent vegetables from coming into contact with dirty surfaces again, set up a **cleaning station**:

- Use basins or buckets to separate **dirty water** from **clean water**.
- Prepare a **clean table** on which to place the washed vegetables.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Organiser une station de nettoyage

pages.title: Step 3: Store effectively
pages.text: Third step: set up a healthy, cool and protected storage space, and monitor your produce daily.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Étape 3 : Stocker efficacement

pages.title: Preparing a good storage place
pages.text:
Prepare a good storage place by following three essential rules:

- **Shaded and cool**: choose a place protected from the sun and heat.
- **Clean**: sweep and wash the space before using it.
- **Pest-free**: protect the place from insects, animals and rodents.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Préparer un bon lieu de stockage

pages.title: Properly arranging and labeling produce
pages.text:
Arrange your produce properly:

- Store only **healthy vegetables**: no damaged, dirty or rotten produce.
- Do not place them directly on the ground: use **baskets** or **shelves**.
- Cover them with a **damp cloth** to keep them fresh.
- Do not pile them up too much, to avoid heat build-up and crushing.
- Write on a **label** the harvest date, the name of the produce and the place or field of origin. This helps you manage your stocks better and reassures your buyers.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Installer et étiqueter correctement les produits

pages.title: Checking and ventilating the storage every day
pages.text:
Every day, carry out two simple checks:

- **Inspect your produce**: immediately remove any that are starting to spoil to prevent them from contaminating the others.
- **Ventilate regularly**: open the doors or windows for a few hours each day to prevent mold.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Contrôler et aérer le stockage chaque jour

pages.title: Step 4: Transport without damage
pages.text: Fourth step: adopt good habits to bring your harvests from the field to the storage or selling place without damaging them.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Étape 4 : Transporter sans dégâts

pages.title: The rules for damage-free transport
pages.text:
When your vegetables leave the field, they must be transported with care. Poor transport can spoil your entire harvest:

- Avoid plastic bags; use **baskets**, **basins** or **ventilated crates** instead to avoid heat and suffocation.
- Do not pack the vegetables tightly, so they can breathe and are not crushed. Place the most fragile ones on top.
- Transport **early in the morning** or **at the end of the day** to avoid the heat.
- Transport **quickly**: the shorter the journey, the better.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les règles d’un transport sans dégâts

pages.title: Conclusion: preserving the quality of your harvests
pages.text: Harvesting at the right time, sorting, washing and packing cleanly, then storing in the shade and transporting quickly: these are simple but essential practices to **preserve the quality of your vegetables** and **make the most of all your work**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Conclusion : préserver la qualité de vos récoltes
